title: How guyed masts stay upright
examples: How do tall radio masts stay up?

forces.label: Wind push
forces.ask: How do tall radio masts stay up?

forces.label: Weight and guy pull
forces.ask: Why can a guyed mast be so thin?

explain.say: A guyed mast is a tall, thin steel lattice that could never stand alone in the wind. Wind pushes on it sideways, trying to bend it over.

forces.label: Wind push
forces.ask: How do tall radio masts stay up?

forces.label: Weight and guy pull
forces.ask: Why can a guyed mast be so thin?

explain.say: Steel cables called guy wires run from several heights on the mast down to anchors in the ground, spread out in three or more directions. Whichever way the wind blows, some guys pull back against it.

forces.label: Wind push
forces.ask: How do tall radio masts stay up?

forces.label: Weight and guy pull
forces.ask: Why can a guyed mast be so thin?

explain.say: The guys pull down as well as sideways, so the slim mast is squeezed from above, in compression. Because it is braced at many points along its height, it does not buckle even though it is very thin.

forces.label: Wind push
forces.ask: How do tall radio masts stay up?

forces.label: Weight and guy pull
forces.ask: Why can a guyed mast be so thin?

explain.say: The mast often stands on a small pivot on a concrete footing, which pushes up on it. Guyed masts are the cheapest way to build extremely tall, light structures for radio and TV.

faq.q: How do tall radio masts stay up?
faq.a: Most very tall masts are guyed: steel cables run from points up the mast to anchors in the ground all around, holding it upright the way ropes hold a tent pole.
asks: How does a guyed mast work?

faq.a: Guy wires are tightened steel cables that brace a mast against wind from any direction. Sets of guys at several heights stop the slim mast bending or buckling.

faq.q: Why can a guyed mast be so thin?
faq.a: The guys support it at many points, so each section between them is short and cannot buckle. The mast mostly just carries a squeezing force down to its base.
asks: Why don't guyed masts need wide bases?

faq.q: What happens if a guy wire breaks?
faq.a: The mast can lose its sideways support and may bend and collapse, so guys and anchors are inspected regularly. The Warsaw Radio Mast, once the world's tallest structure, fell in 1991 while a guy wire was being replaced.
asks: Can a guyed mast fall over?

faq.q: What is the tallest guyed mast?
faq.a: The KVLY-TV mast in North Dakota is about 629 metres tall, one of the tallest structures ever built and the tallest guyed mast standing today.
asks: Which is the tallest mast in the world?

facts: The KVLY-TV mast in North Dakota, completed in 1963, is about 629 metres tall.
The Warsaw Radio Mast in Poland, 646 metres tall, was the world's tallest structure until it collapsed in 1991.

quiz.say: Why does a guyed mast have guy wires going out in at least three directions?
quiz.show: Guys go out in three or more directions so…

options.show: Wind from any side is resisted
options.say: Wind from any side is resisted

quiz.why: Cables can only pull, so they must be spread around the mast to resist wind from every direction.

wrong.1: Looks are not the reason; the cables only pull, so they are needed all round.
wrong.2: Birds may perch on them, but that is not why they are there.
